fact: 1917年4月6日，美国国会通过决议，正式对德国宣战，结束自1914年8月以来的中立。宣战时美国陆军只有约10万志愿兵，按欧洲标准属于极小的军队；此后一年半内约480万人服役，其中过半为征召入伍。

sources.title: Library of Congress, Headlines and Heroes: The Draft in World War I
sources.quote: The reason for the Selective Service Act, though, was that American men had not volunteered en masse or certainly not in the numbers needed to raise, train, and deploy an army quickly after the United States declared war on Germany on April 6, 1917.

sources.title: U.S. National Archives, Prologue: The origins of America's Unlucky Lottery
sources.quote: On April 6, 1917, the United States formally joined World War I ... America entered the war with a tiny army by European standards. We had just 100,000 volunteer troops ... By the war's end in November 1918, 24 million American men had registered for the draft, and of the 4.8 million American troops who served in World War I, more than half had been conscripted.

fact: 1917年5月18日，美国国会通过《选征兵役法》，授权总统临时扩充军队；6月5日举行第一次登记，对象为21至31岁男子，登记卡要求填写住址、出生地、是否公民或已声明入籍意向、职业、雇主、受抚养人，以及是否申请免役。数月内有逾1000万人完成登记。

sources.title: U.S. National Archives, World War I Selective Service System Draft Registration Cards（M1509 说明）
sources.quote: On May 18, 1917, the Selective Service Act was passed authorizing the President to increase temporarily the military establishment of the United States. ... The first, on June 5, 1917, was for all men between the ages of 21 and 31.

sources.title: U.S. National Archives, Prologue: The origins of America's Unlucky Lottery
sources.quote: The new Selective Service Act compelled all men from ages 21 to 30 to register with the Selective Service System. More than 10 million men were registered with the service within several months of the law's passage.

fact: 1917年6月15日，美国《反间谍法》生效（40 Stat. 217）。该法规定：以损害美国或利于外国为目的传递国防信息者，最高可判20年；战时犯此类行为者可判死刑或30年以下监禁；散布虚假报告以妨碍军队作战、煽动军内不服从、或故意阻挠征兵者，可处1万美元以下罚金或20年以下监禁。1918年5月16日的《煽动法》修正案进一步把批评政府、国旗与军队的言论入罪。

sources.title: Cornell Legal Information Institute, Gorin v. United States, 312 U.S. 19（判决书引用《反间谍法》原文）
sources.quote: Espionage Act of June 15, 1917, c. 30, 40 Stat. 217 ... shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than twenty years: Provided, That whoever shall violate the provisions of subsection (a) of this section in time of war shall be punished by death or by imprisonment for not more than thirty years

sources.title: United States v. Binder, 253 F. 978（1918，引用该法第3条）
sources.quote: Whoever, when the United States is at war, shall wilfully make or convey false reports or false statements with intent to interfere with the operation or success of the military or naval forces of the United States ... shall be punished by a fine of not more than $10,000 or imprisonment for not more than twenty years, or both. 40 Stat. 219, c. 30.

fact: 1917年8月10日，美国通过《杠杆食品与燃料管制法》（Lever Food and Fuel Control Act），授予总统管制食品生产、商品价格、原材料与燃料的广泛权力。赫伯特·胡佛出任美国食品管理局局长，推行的是自愿节约——「无麦日」「无肉日」——而非强制配给；美国本土在1917年没有实行面包配给卡制度。

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Labor, World War I
sources.quote: The Lever Act and the Fuel Control Act of 1917 gave President Wilson unmatched power over food production, commodity prices, raw materials, and the nation's fuel resources.

sources.title: InflationCalculator, Inflation in 1917（引 BLS 与 USPS 数据）
sources.quote: Herbert Hoover takes charge of the U.S. Food Administration Appointed in August under the newly passed Lever Food and Fuel Control Act, Hoover led a campaign for voluntary conservation, wheatless and meatless days, rather than mandatory rationing, to keep American troops and Allied civilians fed as food prices climbed with everything else.

fact: 1917年4月24日，美国国会通过《紧急贷款法》，授权财政部长发行总额不超过50亿美元、利率不超过3.5%的债券。财政部于5月14日推出第一笔「自由公债」，数额20亿美元，年息3.5%，期限30年，可转换为后续更高利率的债券；认购至6月15日结束，认购总额约30.35亿美元，超额约52%。1918年3月，第一笔自由公债在市场上的价格约为面值的97.86%。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica 1922, Volume 31, p.799（Wikisource 全文）
sources.quote: Congress, April 24 1917, 18 days after the declaration of a state of war, authorized the Secretary of the Treasury to issue bonds of the United States to the extent of $5,000,000,000. These Liberty Loan Bonds carried interest at the rate of 3 1/2% per annum, were tax-exempt ... He fixed upon the amount of $2,000,000,000, and offered the loan to the public May 17 1917 ... This first offering closed June 15 1917, with subscriptions by 4,000,000 people aggregating $3,035,226,850.

sources.title: Financial History Review, The original Operation Twist: the War Finance Corporation's war bond purchases, 1918–1920
sources.quote: The First Liberty Loan Act, passed on 24 April 1917, authorized the Treasury to issue $5 billion worth of bonds at a rate less than or equal to 3.5 percent interest. The Treasury issued $2 billion of bonds on 14 May 1917, that were to mature in 1947 ... it was oversubscribed by 52 percent ... at the beginning of March 1918, the First Liberty bond at 3.5 percent was selling at 97.86

fact: 1917年10月3日，美国《战时税收法》签署生效：大幅提高所得税率，创设针对战时利润的「超额利润税」，并把一等邮件邮资从2美分提高到3美分，自11月2日起施行——这是1885年以来首次调整邮票价格。战争经费的来源被设计为约三分之一来自税收、三分之二来自向公众借款。

sources.title: InflationCalculator, Inflation in 1917（引 USPS 历史邮资与 BLS 数据）
sources.quote: The War Revenue Act raises taxes and postage to pay for the war Signed October 3, 1917, the act sharply raised income tax rates, created a new excess-profits tax on wartime earnings, and raised first-class postage from 2 cents to 3 cents effective November 2, the first change to the stamp price since 1885.

sources.title: Federal Reserve History, Liberty Bonds（Richard Sutch）
sources.quote: For this war, the federal government relied on a mix of one-third new taxes and two-thirds borrowing from the general population. Very little new money was created.

fact: 1917年7月，伍德罗·威尔逊政府设立战时工业委员会（War Industries Board），由华尔街投机商伯纳德·巴鲁克领导，作为工业动员的中枢，通过谈判「保证企业利润的公平价格」来换取军需品增产。1917年9月21日，该委员会的定价委员会与主要铜生产商达成协议、经总统批准，把铜价固定为每磅23.5美分（纽约离岸价），比当时市价低约3美分，并规定四个月后可依证据复议。

sources.title: The New York Times, FIX COPPER PRICE AT 23 1-2 CENTS（1917-09-21）
sources.quote: President Wilson today approved an agreement entered into by the War Industries Board, by which the United States Government, its allies and the public will obtain copper at twenty-three and a half cents a pound, free on board New York. The price is subject to revision after four months ... The price of twenty-three and a half cents, about three cents below the prevailing market, was fixed by agreement between the Government and the leading copper producers.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Labor, World War I
sources.quote: By the summer of 1917, President Woodrow Wilson's administration had established the War Industries Board (WIB)—under the leadership of the Wall Street stock speculator Bernard M. Baruch—to serve as the center of industrial mobilization. WIB war contracts ensured a rapid increase in production by negotiating fair prices that guaranteed company profits.

fact: 1917年4月美国参战后，航运委员会及其子公司紧急船队公司（Emergency Fleet Corporation）启动大规模造船计划；1917年9月13日，紧急船队公司与美国国际公司签约，在费城特拉华河对岸的霍格岛（Hog Island）修建拥有50个船台的大型船厂，同时订造50艘7500载重吨的标准货船，计划18个月内造200艘。整个计划最终涉及2318艘船，但绝大多数在停战后才下水。战时运价同步飙升：棉花每吨运费从0.35美元涨到1917年的6.10美元。

sources.title: Sea History（National Maritime Historical Society）, A Century of the Jones Act
sources.quote: An emergency shipbuilding program, authorized under the Shipping Act of 1916 and the US Shipping Board (USSB), led to the creation of the Emergency Fleet Corporation (EFC). ... the USSB and EFC oversaw a program that resulted in 2,318 ships. ... the massive Hog Island ship fabrication facility ... had fifty ways, but its 122 ships were all completed after the Armistice. ... the price to ship a ton of cotton jumped from $0.35/ton to $6.10/ton by 1917.

sources.title: Shipscribe, EFC Design 1022 (Hog Island Type A): Notes & Illustrations
sources.quote: on 13 September 1917 the EFC contracted with AIC for the construction by a subsidiary, the American International Shipbuilding Company, of an immense shipyard with 50 building ways in a 'dismal swampy place' named Hog Island on the Delaware River across from the Philadelphia Navy Yard ... it also contracted for 50 11.5-knot Design 1022 cargo ships ... with a plan to build 200 of this type in the next 18 months.

fact: 1917年美国消费者物价指数年均值为12.8（1983=100），较1916年的10.9上涨约17.8%，是当时有记录以来最快的年度涨幅；另一套以1967年为基期的口径记为17.4%。战时需求、男性入伍造成的劳动力短缺与航运中断共同推高物价。食品与服装涨幅高于总体，房租涨幅相对温和。

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, Consumer Price Index, 1913-（BLS 历史序列）
InflationCalculator, Inflation in 1917（BLS CPI-U 历史）
sources.quote: Consumer prices climb 17.4% for the year Wartime demand, labor shortages as men left for the military, and disrupted shipping combined to produce the fastest annual price increase in the CPI's history to that point, more than double 1916's already sharp 7.9% rise.

fact: 1917年美国造船厂工人工资创当时新高。1918年1月参议院辩论引用的某大型船厂工资表显示，铆工个体周薪从7.24美元到172.11美元不等，平均约90美元/周；同期该厂1917年招入1.8万人，只有1.1万人在工作数日后返岗，劳动力流动率极高。1918年2月造船业劳资仲裁把特拉华河与巴尔的摩地区木工日薪定为5.60美元。

sources.title: Congressional Record, Senate, 1918（GovInfo, 65th Congress）
sources.quote: The wages paid in the table noted are not the wages of the riveting gang, but the individual wages of the individual riveters and fitters. ... These men averaged pay $90 a week each. ... In this yard 18,000 men have hired during 1917 and only 11,000 have returned to work after working a few days.

sources.title: The New York Times, WILSON WILL TRY TO ADJUST STRIKE OF SHIP WORKERS（1918-02-17）
sources.quote: The jump to $5.60 a day in the Delaware River and Baltimore district represents an increase proportionately greater, when the wages now being paid to the carpenters in the district are taken into consideration.
